Atlas syncs data from the source to the destination cluster until you cut your applications over to the destination Atlas cluster.

evidence.quote: Atlas keeps track of the latest execution time for each Trigger and guarantees that each event is processed at least once.
However, when some failure or error conditions occur, Triggers may deliver duplicate events.
However, when things go wrong, Kafka can only guarantee that consumers receive every message at least once.

However, the MongoDB connectors will resume from the last offset recorded by the earlier processes, which means that the new replacement tasks may generate some of the same change events that were processed just prior to the crash.

statements.statement: Atlas documents at-least-once event processing and possible duplicate delivery after failures.
Debezium documents replay after a crash before offset persistence.
Neither establishes exactly-once external side effects by itself; design downstream effects to tolerate repeats.

edits.rationale: Atlas guarantees at-least-once processing and may deliver duplicates on failure. Debezium documents that after a crash it resumes from the last recorded offset and may regenerate events, and that it provides at-least-once delivery when things go wrong. Neither source claims exactly-once external side effects under failure.
